findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources implement the conventional two-candidate generalized Boyer-Moore algorithm. Candidate cancellation followed by exact verification is correct, clear, O(n)-time, and O(1)-auxiliary-space, and its names describe genuine voting concepts; no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and native class method have the same two slots, branch order, simultaneous cancellation, strict threshold, candidate deduplication, and result construction. Their only differences are the required LeetCode class wrapper and local type annotation.

The former benchmark used only three distinct values, so repeated full-array counting remained linear in its input shape. Legal 16/64/256-value all-distinct tiers now force candidate churn and expose that slower class. The protected source passes at -0.00 relative exponent; a correct count-every-distinct-value implementation passes every output and fails only scaling at +1.13 with a 50.83x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach accurately derives the at-most-two bound, explains triple cancellation and the required verification pass, states the output-excluded O(1) auxiliary-space convention, and now labels short-array and duplicate-candidate boundaries explicitly.
